newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus sees bigger Russian crude oil supplies.
newsitem.headline: Belarus sees bigger Russian crude oil supplies.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has agreed to supply two Belarussian refineries with an extra 300,000 tonnes of Russian crude oil a month, Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko said on Wednesday.

"I asked the president of the Russian Federation about delivering a small, extra quantity of oil for refining in Belarus at two oil refining plants -- that is, about an additional 300,000 (tonnes) every month," Lukashenko told a news conference after meeting Yeltsin.
He said he had won Yeltsin's support for the scheme and that some of the refined oil would be exported to Western markets.
But he gave no details on how the former Soviet republic of Belarus would pay for the supplies or when they would begin.
The crude will likely be refined at two large refineries, one in Novopolotsk, which has a capacity of 25 million tonnes a year, and one in Mozyr, which has a 15 million tonne annual capacity.
Belarus needs about 12 million tonnes of crude oil to meet annual domestic demand.
